title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium): hold reports for all cases
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the roadmap's planned release from Microsoft's documented public preview. The report permissions, commands, subscription requirement and reporting limitations are supported; the permission path needs one heading restored and the summary should omit an unrepresented control gap.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans out-of-the-box reports about all legal holds associated with eDiscovery cases.
claims.quote: Out-of-the-box reports that contain information about all legal holds associated with eDiscovery cases in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal.

claims.quote: Sort and filter your view based on various criteria

claims.claim: The planned reports support filtering.
claims.quote: Sort and filter your view based on various criteria

claims.claim: The planned reports allow downloading aggregated information for further analysis.
claims.quote: download the aggregated information for further analysis.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents the hold report as a public preview.
claims.quote: The hold report is in public preview and provides a tenant-wide summary of hold policies for all eDiscovery cases.

claims.claim: The documented report is a built-in view of existing eDiscovery holds in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: access a built-in report with information on all holds associated with eDiscovery cases in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The report covers all hold policies within the tenant.
claims.quote: The hold report shows the data locations and reports on all hold policies within the tenant.

claims.claim: The report lists locations in hold policies whether those policies are enabled or disabled.
claims.quote: It lists all locations that are part of those hold policies, whether enabled or disabled.

claims.claim: Users with eDiscovery Administrator permissions can view the hold report.

claims.fix: Set controls[0].ui.path and its rendered table path to 'Settings > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users'. The cited page places Choose users under Manage eDiscovery Manager.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The report can show the user who last modified a hold policy.
claims.quote: Policy last modified by: Shows the user that last modified the hold policy.

claims.claim: The item count counts locations within hold policies, so a location held under several policies appears and counts several times.
claims.quote: If the same location is placed on hold under different policies, the same location appears multiple times in the report under the respective case and hold policy and contributes to multiple item counts.

claims.claim: For Policy failed, Microsoft advises creating a rule and resyncing the policy.
claims.quote: Policy failed: Indicates that the policy is set up incorrectly. ... To ensure these policies are enforced, create a rule and resync the policy.

claims.claim: Learn provides a Security & Compliance PowerShell script as an automated reporting alternative, using Get-CaseHoldPolicy with DistributionDetail.
claims.quote: Step 1: Connect to Security & Compliance PowerShell ... $policies = Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Case $cc.Name | % { Get-CaseHoldPolicy $_.Name -Case $_.CaseId -DistributionDetail }

claims.claim: The script covers all cases for an eDiscovery Administrator but only accessible cases for an eDiscovery Manager.
claims.quote: To generate a report on all eDiscovery cases in your organization, you need to be an eDiscovery Administrator in your organization. If you're an eDiscovery Manager, the report only includes information about the cases that you can access.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not support the sample script under any standard support programme or service.
claims.quote: The sample scripts provided in this article aren't supported under any Microsoft standard support program or service.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Generating and accessing the report requires an organisation subscription supporting premium eDiscovery features.
claims.quote: Your organization must have an organization subscription that supports premium eDiscovery features to generate and access the hold report.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Premium eDiscovery entitlement is available through Office 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5 or related E5 add-on subscriptions, as reflected in the mixed licensing model.
claims.quote: If your organization has an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 subscription (or related E5 add-on subscriptions), you can further manage cases and analyze content by using premium eDiscovery features.

claims.claim: For analysis with premium features, the permissions page allows Microsoft Purview Suite or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on licences for users with Office 365 E1 or Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3.
claims.quote: users with an Office 365 E1 or an Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3 license can be assigned a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.
